title: DPF response to BoE systemic stablecoins discussion paper
original_scope: Complete primary page archived; not yet full semantic review.
pinpoint: Opening key messages; Q3 business-model discussion; Q11 backing assets; complete Q12 remuneration answer; Q24–25 holding limits; Q26–27 issuer structure/business models.
review_pinpoint: Opening key messages; Q3 business-model discussion; Q11 backing assets; complete Q12 remuneration answer; Q24–25 holding limits; Q26–27 issuer structure/business models.
finding: DPF understands the transactional rationale and recognises credit-creation concerns from deposit outflows, but warns against making payments the only permitted use. It identifies long-term competitive disadvantage to nonbanks from the ban combined with limits and seeks flexibility for emerging models. It separately contests non-remunerated central-bank backing and the resulting transition cliff. This is a qualified position, not unreserved support for either a blanket ban or unrestricted remuneration.

title: ICAEW REP015/24 DP23/4: Stablecoins

review_pinpoint: Representation15/24, issued5February2024; PDF pp1–4 key messages and paras5–13; pp9–11 Q4–6, particularly paras54–58; adjacent Q7 paras59–62.
finding: ICAEW accepts the practical advantages of issuer-retained returns for a payments business, but expressly contemplates alternative models passing interest and returns to holders while charging transaction fees. It also identifies yield/stability conflicts and the potential viability cliff between FCA reserve income and unremunerated Bank reserves.
